title: [Bug report tool] "Generate bug report" zip leaks the Mouse Without Borders SecurityKey in clear text (runner log + MouseWithoutBorders.backup), and includes machine names / LAN IPs without an option to remove them

judgment.rationale: The report gives reproducible archive-generation steps and names the unredacted locations. Current main confirms both causes: raw settings-payload logging and a collector that redacts only configured file paths after recursively copying settings and logs.
evidence: The reporter identifies the primary settings file as redacted but reports the pairing secret in a runner settings-broadcast log and a legacy backup settings file.
Current main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 logs the complete JSON payload in src/runner/settings_window.cpp::dispatch_received_json.
Current BugReportTool/Main.cpp recursively copies settings and LocalLow logs, then scrubs only paths in escapeInfo; the map includes only the primary MouseWithoutBorders\\settings.json path.
The package is intended for public issue attachment, so verification must use synthetic test data and inspect the completed ZIP.

Re-read the edited 2026-11-06 report: it supplies concrete runner-log and backup-file examples, while secret and identifying values are represented only by placeholders; no additional comments were present.
judgment.recommended_action: Remove sensitive values from runner logging and make archive redaction cover all copied Mouse Without Borders settings backups and logs; add a synthetic archive regression test.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current source and the reporter's concrete file paths establish an applicable secret-redaction fix; anonymization of other identifiers remains a separate product/privacy decision.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Mouse Without Borders secrets out of bug-report archives
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The runner logs the complete settings IPC payload, while the bug-report tool recursively collects settings and logs but redacts the pairing key only at one exact settings-file path. The collector therefore includes sensitive values from runner logs and copied backup settings.
plan: Stop logging raw settings IPC payloads; log only non-sensitive change metadata, or redact sensitive properties such as SecurityKey before serialization to the runner log.
Extend archive sanitization to cover every copied Mouse Without Borders settings JSON, including legacy backup folders, and scrub sensitive values from collected logs before they enter the ZIP.
Add a regression fixture with a synthetic pairing key in the primary settings file, a backup settings file, and a runner log; assert that no copy of the synthetic value survives in the final package.
Track anonymization of machine, network, user-name, and SID data as a separate privacy decision so it does not delay the secret-redaction fix.
verification: Generate a test report from a fixture containing only a synthetic secret and verify that the final ZIP has no occurrence in any settings, backup, or log entry.
Confirm that the primary settings file remains redacted and ordinary diagnostic fields needed for triage are still present.
Run focused BugReportTool tests and inspect the extracted test archive; never validate with a real pairing key.

confidence.rationale: The issue names the exact unredacted files, and current upstream main confirms raw settings-payload logging, recursive collection, and path-specific redaction that omits backup files and logs.

issue_context.summary: Bug-report packages can include the Mouse Without Borders pairing secret in copied runner logs and legacy backup settings, even though the primary settings file is redacted.
known_information: The reporter gives a repeatable package-generation scenario on PowerToys 0.103.3052.0 and identifies a runner settings-broadcast log and a legacy backup settings file as unredacted locations.
Current PowerToys main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 logs the full settings JSON in src/runner/settings_window.cpp::dispatch_received_json.

The bug-report tool recursively copies settings and LocalLow logs, then scrubs only explicitly listed relative paths; its redaction map covers the primary MouseWithoutBorders\\settings.json but not backup settings or runner logs.
The issue also reports machine names, LAN addresses, user-name paths, and an account SID in the package; no actual identifiers or secret values are retained here.
inferences: Avoiding raw secret logging and redacting every collected copy provide complementary protection against future archives containing pairing secrets.
Anonymizing identifying metadata is a distinct product/privacy decision from preventing the pairing secret from entering the archive.
issue_context.analysis: The current source and the reporter's file-level reproduction support a concrete credential-redaction fix. Validate with synthetic data only; do not use the attached archive or a real pairing key.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report; its examples contain placeholders rather than actual key values.

Read current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368: settings_window.cpp logs the full incoming JSON payload; BugReportTool/Main.cpp recursively copies settings and LocalLow logs and scrubs only paths in the explicit escapeInfo map.
Confirmed that the redaction map targets only the primary MouseWithoutBorders\\settings.json path, so copied backup files and runner logs are outside that rule.
Did not download or inspect the reporter's uploaded archive.
Re-read the edited report at its current 2026-11-06 revision; it adds no unredacted secret or identifier value to this artifact.
